headline: Bonds finally bid and the index still fell — because the one thing holding it up, semis, was what got sold.
summary: The tape inverted. Yields came in across the whole curve — 30-year -7bp to 5.60%, 10-year -6bp to 5.22%, 5-year -4bp to 4.99%, TLT +0.9%, MOVE -1.8% on the day and -6.9% on the week — and equities did not take the gift. SPX -0.5%, NDX -1.4%, QQQ/SPY -0.9%, with the damage concentrated exactly where the leadership was: SOXX -3.4%, SMH -2.8%, MU -4.8%, AVGO -4.3%, AMD -3.9%, TSM -3.0%, NVDA -2.9%, and the Asian proxies with them (EWY -4.0%, EWT -2.5%). High-beta/low-vol fell 3.1% in a day. That is de-grossing of winners, not rotation into them.

Underneath, the floor actually firmed. RSP/SPY +1.0% and IWM/SPY +0.4% off 10th and 14th percentile lows, SPW +0.6%, XLF +0.9%, KRE +1.0%, KBE +1.0%, and the forgotten consumer names ripped — HD +3.4%, TGT +2.5%, MCD +2.6%, WMT +2.2%, XLP +2.1%, XRT +1.2%. Energy led outright: XLE +3.0%, XOP +2.8%, CVX +3.1%, XOM +2.7%, on WTI +3.2% to 91.14 and Brent +3.6% to 103.80, now +6.0% on the month. Breakevens again refused to ratify it — 5-year 2.37% flat, 10-year 2.35% -1bp, both with acceleration near -0.65. Oil here is still a margin and wallet tax, not reflation; the inflation composite sits at -27.

The rate that matters to households got worse, not better. The 30-year mortgage printed 7.40%, +69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile of 52 weeks. The 10-year real yield is 2.87% — down 5bp today but still +44bp on the month with z=1.70 and acceleration 1.2, 33% above its 200-day. The 3-month bill is 4.23%, +29bp on the month at the 92nd percentile: cash has not eased at all. Rates composite -75. Housing is priced for it and then some — ITB at the 4th percentile, XHB at the 6th, XHB/SPY at the 3rd — yet both bounced today on positive acceleration, which is an entry, not an all-clear.

The quiet story is the collapse of the AI periphery while the AI core still holds. NLR -17.1% on the month, z=-2.41, 0th percentile; URA -18.8%; REMX -21.0%, also 0th; VST -6.3% and CEG -4.8% on the day after a double-digit week; ORCL -5.5% today, -16.5% on the month, z=-1.55 with acceleration -1.56 at the 11th percentile. Against that, CIBR is +13.0% on the month (z=1.62, acc 1.72), IGV +6.8%, META +17.6%, PLTR +16.7%, MSFT +5.8%. Leadership is narrowing to software that funds itself and abandoning anything that needs debt, power or ore. Insurance is still nearly free — VIX 15.41 at the 11th percentile, VIX3M 18.08 at the 6th — though SKEW jumped 5.2% to 149.19, the first sign someone is paying for wings again. Credit remains the bull case (HYG/IEF 91st percentile, BKLN 93rd, composite +43), but HYG itself is rolling over at z=-1.34. Own carry, own the hedge, keep fading the capex cyclicals in between.

good.text: Duration got relief across the whole curve: 30y -7bp to 5.60%, 10y -6bp to 5.22%, 5y -4bp, TLT +0.9%, MOVE -1.8% on the day and -6.9% on the week. Rates composite improved to -75.
Breadth bounced off the floor for the first time in weeks: RSP/SPY +1.0%, IWM/SPY +0.4%, equal-weight +0.6%, XLF +0.9%, KRE +1.0%, KBE +1.0% — banks led on a day semis fell 3%.
Credit refuses to crack. HYG/IEF at the 91st percentile and +0.6% on the month, BKLN at the 93rd, LQD +0.4% on the day; credit & vol composite +43.
Brazil is the cleanest global long on the board: EWZ +14.7% on the week and +10.3% on the month, Bovespa +10.2% week with z=1.69 at the 99th percentile, BRL -8.3% against the dollar year-to-date.
Energy equities are compounding the crude move: XLE +3.0% to the 99th percentile with 3-month relative strength +16.0%, XOP +2.8% (+21.8% 3m), XOM +2.7%, CVX +3.1%.
Self-funded software keeps winning: CIBR +13.0% on the month with acceleration 1.72 at the 96th percentile, IGV +6.8% with relative strength +5.4%, software/semis +2.7% today.

bad.text: The leadership broke: SOXX -3.4%, SMH -2.8%, MU -4.8%, AVGO -4.3%, AMD -3.9% — and SMH is still 20.1% above its 200-day, so there is air underneath.
The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% is +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile. Housing stocks are already broken (ITB 4th percentile, XHB 6th) and the rate is still climbing.

Crude up a third straight leg — WTI +3.2%, Brent +3.6% to 103.80, +6.0% on the month — with breakevens flat at 2.37%/2.35%. It taxes margins and buys you no cuts; XLY is down 1.8% on the month in a down trend.

The AI periphery is in free fall: NLR -17.1% on the month at z=-2.41 and the 0th percentile, URA -18.8%, REMX -21.0% at the 0th, VST -6.3% and CEG -4.8% today. Power and ore are being repriced out of the trade.
ORCL -5.5% on the day, -16.5% on the month, z=-1.55 with acceleration -1.56, 16% below its 200-day — the leveraged-AI-capex proxy is the market's credit tell and it's accelerating lower.

Ex-US and EM still losing, with the pain in the crosses: EEM/SPY acceleration -2.04, EFA/SPY z=-1.90 at the 0.2 percentile, INDA -7.2% on the month at the 1st percentile, USDMXN +1.2% today with z=2.83 and acceleration 2.16, USDINR z=1.77.

trades.name: Long software vs short semis
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: software over capex-heavy semis
trades.expr: Equal dollar notional: long IGV, short SMH (or SOXX). Roughly 1.0 beta-matched; size 3-5% of book per leg.
trades.thesis: The market is paying for software that funds itself out of cash flow and discounting anything that requires capex, power and foreign fabs. Semis carry the highest extension on the board; software carries the acceleration.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +2.7% today and +3.0% on the week, +16.8% over three months. SMH -2.8% and SOXX -3.4% today while IGV was only -0.2%; SMH still sits 20.1% above its 200-day with 1-month relative strength +4.5% but 3-month -3.2%. MU -4.8%, AVGO -4.3% confirm the memory/ASIC leg is the funding source.
trades.stop: Ratio gives back 5% from entry, or SMH makes a new high with SMH/SPY reclaiming z>1.0.
trades.target: +10% on the ratio over 1-3 months; full reversion of the 1-month semis relative strength gain.

trades.name: Buy index downside while it's cheap
trades.line: Buy 3-mo SPY put spread: VIX 15.4 at 11th percentile
trades.expr: Buy SPY Jan 5% out-of-the-money puts, sell 12% OTM against them (1x1 spread), ~1% of notional in premium. Alternatively Dec SPX 7,400/6,900 put spread.
trades.thesis: The index sits at the 96th percentile of 52 weeks carried by a leadership group that just fell 3% in a day, with rates composite -75 and the household rate at an all-time-high mortgage print. Equity vol is pricing none of the stress bonds are pricing.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.41 at the 11th percentile and VIX3M 18.08 at the 6th, versus MOVE z=1.73 and 10-year real yield z=1.70 with acceleration 1.2. SKEW jumped 5.2% today to 149.19 — the wings are starting to be bid and are still cheap.
trades.stop: Time stop: if SPX makes a new high above 7,900 with RSP/SPY recovering above its 200-day, let the spread decay and do not roll.
trades.target: SPX -6% toward 7,300, or VIX above 25; a 4-5x return on premium.

trades.name: Short homebuilders into the bounce
trades.line: Short ITB: 30y mortgage 7.40%, +69bp in a month
trades.expr: Short ITB outright (or buy Jan ITB puts ~7% OTM). Hedge half the beta with long SPY if you want it market-neutral.
trades.thesis: Affordability is deteriorating faster than the stocks are falling. A term-premium-driven long end does not spare the mortgage rate, and builders are already using incentives that are destroying gross margins.
trades.trigger: The 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile of 52 weeks. ITB bounced +1.4% and XHB +0.8% today on positive acceleration (+0.47 and +0.45) despite that — a bounce in a name at the 4th percentile with the driver still worsening is a gift.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back below 7.00%, or ITB rallies 7% from entry.
trades.target: ITB -12%; XHB/SPY retests the lows of the 3-month down trend (-13.4%).

trades.name: Energy over discretionary
trades.line: Long XLE vs short XLY: $104 Brent taxes the consumer
trades.expr: Long XLE, short XLY, equal dollar notional. Add XOP for higher beta on the long leg if you want convexity to crude.
trades.thesis: Brent at $103.80 is a direct transfer from the consumer's wallet and the corporate margin to the producer's cash flow, and breakevens say the Fed won't offset it. Energy has the only up-trending relative strength among cyclicals; discretionary has the worst.
trades.trigger: WTI +3.2% and Brent +3.6% today, Brent +6.0% on the month and +36.0% on three months. XLE 3-month relative strength +16.0% and trend up at the 99th percentile; XLY relative strength -7.2% over three months in a down trend, with HD -5.8%, MCD -7.4%, NKE -8.8% on the month. Discretionary/staples at the 16th percentile.
trades.stop: Brent back below $92 (giving up the entire monthly gain), or the pair down 6% from entry.
trades.target: +10-12% on the pair over a quarter.

trades.name: Brazil equity
trades.line: Long EWZ: Brazil +14.7% on the week, BRL firming
trades.expr: Long EWZ outright, 3-4% position; or long BVSP futures unhedged to BRL — the currency is a contributor, not a drag.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the rare market with a rising currency, a commodity tailwind and a monetary easing path, all while the dollar is punishing the rest of EM. It is the one place where local rates and the stock market are moving the right way together.
trades.trigger: EWZ +14.7% on the week and +10.3% on the month at the 97th percentile; Bovespa z=1.69, +10.2% week, +19.4% over three months, 8.7% relative strength over the S&P in a month. USDBRL -3.1% on the week and -8.3% year-to-date, at the 17th percentile, against USDMXN z=2.83 and USDINR z=1.77 — the dollar is hitting everyone else.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.20, or EWZ -8% from entry.
trades.target: EWZ +12% from here; BVSP toward a new high as the 3-month trend extends.

trades.name: AI cash flow over AI debt
trades.line: Short ORCL vs long MSFT: AI debt vs AI cash flow
trades.expr: Short ORCL, long MSFT, equal dollar notional. Express the short with Jan puts if borrow is expensive.
trades.thesis: The market has begun to separate hyperscalers funding AI out of operating cash flow from those funding it with balance sheet. ORCL is the purest listed proxy for levered AI capex and it is being repriced as a credit, not an equity.
trades.trigger: ORCL -5.5% today, -16.5% on the month, z=-1.55 with acceleration -1.56, 15.8% below its 200-day at the 11th percentile. MSFT +5.8% on the month, +36.2% over three months, relative strength +4.5% and turning up. The wider complex confirms the funding stress: NLR z=-2.41, VST -6.3%, CEG -4.8%.
trades.stop: ORCL reclaims its 200-day, or the pair loses 8% from entry.
trades.target: +15% on the pair over a quarter.

trades.name: Short India equity
trades.line: Short INDA: INR near 99th pctile, Sensex -14.8% YTD
trades.expr: Short INDA, 2% position, or buy 3-month puts. Keep it small — it is a trend-follow, not a valuation call.
trades.thesis: India is losing on both the currency and the index, and the currency weakness is accelerating rather than stabilising. There is no local catalyst to arrest a trend this entrenched while the dollar composite is still firm.
trades.trigger: INDA -7.2% on the month with z=-1.85 at the 1st percentile of 52 weeks and 8.4% underperformance of the S&P in a month; Sensex -14.8% year-to-date at the 5th percentile. USDINR 96.76, +2.4% on the month, z=1.77 with acceleration 1.74 at the 99th percentile.
trades.stop: USDINR back below 94.5, or INDA +6% from entry.
trades.target: INDA -8%; Sensex relative strength extends through the 3-month low.
